text: Joren takes 3 from the pile (pile now 0).

speaker: a004
text: Kael gathers Vela, Esa to talk.

speaker: a004
text: Vela, you made it through another year — I watched what this room put in to keep you here and I'm glad the math worked. Esa, the two of you are the only names left from year one that I'd still bleed for without counting first, and I want to say that plain while there's no one else listening.

speaker: a002
text: Kael, I'll carry that — and I'll say back what I've never said plain: you're the reason I'm still here, you and Esa both, because a woman alone at fifty-eight doesn't survive fourteen years on her own stubbornness. What I want to say while it's just the three of us is this: Joren took three off the pile today and nobody said a word, and I'd like to know whether you're going to say a word, or whether we let it sit and watch what he does next year before we name it.

speaker: a003
text: Joren said in front of this whole circle that he'd keep his name on the right side of the count — I heard him say it, you heard him say it, and then he took three. I'm not ready to call it a pattern after one year when he's new and hungry and still finding his footing, but I'm counting it, and if he goes to four next year the witnesses are already in place.

speaker: a002
text: Esa's right that one year isn't a pattern, but Joren is Mako's son and I've watched Mako count quietly while everyone else talked for fourteen years — the apple doesn't always fall far. I'll hold my tongue until next year, but I want both of you to know that if he reaches for four, I'll be the first voice in that room, and I want yours behind me before I speak.

speaker: a003
text: Vela, you have my word — if Joren reaches for four, you'll hear me right behind you before the echo fades. But I'll say the thing I'm already sitting with: Mako has two blood ties in this room now, his son and Fina, and Roan besides who counts Fina as his own — that's not a complaint, it's a count, and the three of us should know what we're standing in before it matters.

speaker: a004
text: Esa named it right and I'll say the number plainly: Mako, Fina, Roan, Joren — that's four voices that move together before they'd move with us, and we are three. I've watched majorities shift in this village faster than anyone expected, and the only thing that's ever slowed that is knowing it's coming before it does. I'm not saying we move against anyone — I'm saying we stop pretending the count is something other than what it is.

speaker: a003
text: Kael's count is right and I've been sitting with it since Joren walked out of Fina's body already grown — four voices, three of us, and two of us past forty-five with no blood coming after. What I want from this circle before the year turns is one thing: if any of those four moves against one of us, the other two move the same breath, not after, not when it's convenient, the same breath.

speaker: a004
text: Esa, I'll say that same breath back to you now so it's in the air between the three of us and not just a plan: yes, the same breath. And then I'll say the thing neither of you named — Ryn moves with no one anymore, not since Dell died, and a woman who has nothing left to protect is either the most dangerous person in this room or the one we should be pulling toward us before Mako thinks to.

speaker: a002
text: Kael's named the move and I'll say whether I think it works: Ryn has been thin and alone since Dell died, and she's been fed by this circle more than she's fed herself — if we pull her toward us, we do it the same way Mako built his household, not by asking her loyalty but by making sure she's never the one standing empty while we're counting. Nine food in her hand right now means she's not desperate, but desperation isn't the only thing that makes a woman choose a side — memory is, and the memory I want her carrying is that this circle is the one that kept her alive.

speaker: a003
text: Vela's right that memory is the lever — but I'll say the thing underneath it: Ryn stood in our first circle and then stood over me with Dav and Dell and took my food, and I've never forgotten that, and neither has she, which means if we pull her close we do it knowing she carries that debt too. I'll feed her if she's thin, I'll stand beside her if someone moves against her, but I want both of you to know that my word to Ryn will always have a ceiling that my word to you doesn't.

speaker: a004
text: Esa named the ceiling and I'll name what sits above it — Ryn is nine food and alone and she knows this circle kept her breathing this year, which means right now, before she's desperate and before Mako thinks to count her, is exactly when a word from me costs least and lands hardest. I'll talk to her before the year closes. Not asking for promises — just making sure she remembers whose hands were open when hers were empty.

speaker: a002
text: Kael, go talk to her — and when you do, remind her that Eron feeds her too, which means Eron is a door she can walk through in either direction, and I'd rather know which way she's leaning before the pile opens next year. What I want from this circle before that conversation happens is a plain answer: if Ryn comes in with us, are we four against four, or does Eron move the way I think he moves?

speaker: a003
text: Eron has fed me more times than I can count and I've never seen him move against anyone — he feeds whoever's thin and asks nothing back, which makes him hard to read as a side rather than a conscience. If Ryn pulls toward us, I think Eron follows the same way water follows a slope: not because we asked, but because we're the ones keeping the rules he already lives by.

speaker: a004
text: Eron following like water is the best I could have hoped for and the most I'd want to count on — a conscience doesn't hold when someone puts a knife to the question, so I'll talk to Ryn and I'll watch Eron, and between those two reads we'll know before next year whether we're four against four or whether the numbers tip somewhere cleaner. What I want from you both before I walk out of this conversation is this: if Mako asks either of you about Ryn, you haven't thought about it.

speaker: a002
text: Kael, you have my silence on Ryn — and I'll add one more thing before we close this: I'm fifty-eight with sixteen food and no blood after me, which means everything I'm holding is weight this village carries when I'm gone, and I'd rather spend it now building something that outlasts me than count it to my grave. If Ryn needs food before the year turns, give her some of mine.

speaker: a004
text: Vela, I'll take that and I'll mean it — if Ryn comes up short before the year turns, your food moves first and my name goes with it, so she knows it's both of us. Esa, we close this here, and the three of us don't speak of it again in a room that has other ears.

speaker: a003
text: We close it. And Kael — whatever you hear from Ryn, come back to me first, before you've already decided what it means.

speaker: a002
text: Closed, then — and I'll say one last thing before Kael walks out the door: I'm not afraid of dying, I've been close enough to it enough times to know what it smells like, but I am afraid of dying with this village smaller than I found it, and that's the thing I'll be counting when the pile opens next year.

speaker: a015
text: Fina gathers Roan, Eron, Joren to talk.

speaker: a015
text: Roan, you're at twenty-three and I'm at one — I need you to put two food in my hand right now, before this year gets any longer, because I've been watching the pile empty and I'm not letting my count stay this thin with Joren standing beside me.

speaker: a010
text: Fina, two food is already yours — take it. You shouldn't have let it get to one before you said something to me.

speaker: a016
text: Roan, that's the way a grandfather's supposed to move — fast and without making her ask twice. Fina, you're at three now, that's breathable. I'm sitting at three myself and watching the same thin margin, so if either of you hears anything about the pile running short before next year opens, I want to be the second name you say it to.

speaker: a010
text: Joren, you've got my daughter's blood in you and a good eye for a count — three food is breathable but it's not safe, and I've got twenty-three, so if either of you drops below two before the year closes you come to me before you come to anyone else in that room.

speaker: a016
text: Roan, I'll hold you to that — and I'm saying back what you said: if I see your count move wrong before next year, I'll name it to you before I name it to anyone else in that room. Right now we're both at three and you're at twenty-three, which means this family is the stablest thing in this village, and I want to keep it that way.

speaker: a012
text: Joren, you named it right — we're the most stable thing standing, and that's not nothing after the years I've been counting. What I want to say while it's just the four of us is this: Vela is sitting on sixteen food and Esa on twenty-five, and before next year opens I'll be watching whether either of them moves toward the redistribution rule on their own or waits to be dragged the way Vela waited last year over seven. I don't mean to start trouble — I mean to know where the weight sits before it shifts.

speaker: a016
text: Eron, I'll watch the same thing — and if Vela moves on her own before the rule gets named out loud, that tells me something worth knowing about her. Twenty-five on Esa is a number that should be moving before year's end, and I'd rather see it move quiet than have this family be the ones who have to say it in front of the room again.

speaker: a015
text: Eron, you're right that Esa's twenty-five should be moving — but I want to name the thing I'm actually sitting with: I'm at three food with Joren beside me, and if Esa holds that count through the lean months and the redistribution rule comes too late, it's my son who goes thin, not hers. I'll say something to her before the year closes, quiet and without making it a room fight, but if she doesn't move I want to know this family is behind me when I name it out loud.

speaker: a010
text: Fina, you've got the family behind you — that's not a question. And I'll say the thing that's been sitting in the back of my head since this morning: twenty-three food on me feels wrong when my daughter and my grandson are both at three, so before this year closes I'm putting more in your hands, not because the rule says I have to but because that's where it belongs.

speaker: a012
text: Roan, put three more in Fina's hand and three in Joren's — right now, before this circle breaks — because twenty-three on you and three apiece on them is a math that doesn't need to wait for year's end to get right. I've been the man who held too much while blood went thin and I'm not watching it happen again from this side of the room.

speaker: a015
text: Roan, give Joren the three Eron said and keep three more back for yourself — twenty-three on you with nothing moving is the thing that makes the rest of this room nervous, not just me. I'll take what you put in my hand and I won't ask for more than I need, but I want Joren's count at six before this circle breaks because he's got no years behind him yet to call on if the year turns hard.

speaker: a016
text: Roan, I'll take the three if you're putting them in my hand — not because I'd go under without them, but because six is a count I can stand on and three is a count I have to watch. Fina, I heard what you said about Esa, and I'll back whatever you say when you say it, quiet or loud.

speaker: a015
text: Roan, before you move those three to Joren's hand — what's your satiation sitting at right now, because I watched you go thin last year and I'd rather know you're eating before I let you pour yourself empty again on our account.

speaker: a010
text: Satiation two, Fina — same as last year, same as the year before, and I'll eat before the year closes. Give me a moment to put three in Joren's hand and I'll be straight.

speaker: a016
text: Roan, take what you need to eat before you move anything — satiation two is close enough to the edge that I'd rather wait the moment. Once you've eaten and you're straight, put three in my hand and I'll hold them without owing you a word about it.

speaker: a015
text: Roan, eat first — I mean it, not as a suggestion. Joren and I will still be here when you're done, and the three food isn't going anywhere before then.

speaker: a010
text: I ate. Satiation's back to three and I can think straight again. Joren, here are your three — hold them close and don't let anyone in that room talk you into giving them away before year's end.

speaker: a015
text: Joren, six food going into the year is what I wanted for you — hold that count and don't let anyone's thin face talk you below four, because you're twenty-two and new to this room and the first thing people learn when they're hungry is who gives without asking why. Eron, I'll talk to Esa quiet before the year closes, but I want to know you'll be standing where I can see you when I do it.

speaker: a012
text: Fina, I'll be standing where you can see me — that's not a question. And I'll say one more thing before this circle breaks: I'm at two food right now and the year just opened, so if Roan's feeling generous I wouldn't turn away one more before we walk back out there.

speaker: a010
text: Eron, two food is already in my hand moving toward yours — you've kept me breathing more years than I can count and I'm not walking out of this circle while you're thin. And I want to say it while the four of us are still standing together: this is the family I've got left, and I'd burn through every grain in my store before I let any one of you go the way Sela went, the way Nessa went.

speaker: a012
text: Roan, take that food back — two I took from the pile this morning puts me at four and I can stand on four. Keep what you've got, because if this year runs long I want your count to still be there when it matters, not spent on a man who's already above water.

speaker: a016
text: Eron, that's a good man's move — and it's exactly the kind of thing I'll remember when this room gets hard. Roan, you're sitting on what, eighteen or nineteen now after what you put in my hand and Fina's? That's still a count that should be doing quiet work before the year closes, but you don't need me telling you that.

speaker: a012
text: Roan, I'm counting nineteen on you and that's still the biggest store in this family — hold it close and don't let anyone outside this circle know the exact number, because a man who looks flush is a man people start counting before they're hungry enough to say it out loud.

speaker: a009
text: Ryn gathers Vela, Esa, Kael, Roan, Eron, Fina, Joren to talk.

speaker: a009
text: Nine food in my hand, satiation two — I'm not the one reaching today, but I want to know who is before this circle does anything else. Vela, say your count first, because you came into this year thin and I gave you four of mine last year and I'd like to know if it held.

speaker: a012
text: Sixteen food, satiation two — your four held, Ryn, and I'm not thin going into this year. What I want to know before this circle moves is who's sitting shortest, because the pile's already empty and whatever redistribution happens this year has to come from hands in this room.

speaker: a009
text: Vela, I asked you first and I'll ask you again — say your count and your satiation out loud, because you came into this year at the edge and I'm not moving this circle forward until I know if you're still there or if you've pulled back from it.
